title: Latency-aware lossy compression and prompt slimming guide
body:
Context / goal:
Quick, pragmatic notes for field POCs where customer SLO is latency < 250ms p95 for first-token on 4k context, but they also require 75%+ semantic fidelity vs baseline (ft/llm). We need fast knobs for net token-cost reduction and deterministic latency wins that are easy for SEs to demo during workshops.

High-level approach:
- Target the easy wins first: prompt slimming + KH (known-history) prefix caching + shallow quant (8-bit) on non-critical model variants.
- Fall back: introduce lossy compression of long user context via chunk summarization / embedding-index sparsing before the request reaches model.
- Always measure fidelity against small set of user prompts (5–10) that cover edge behaviors.

Experiment matrix (recommended order):
1) Prompt slimming (no model change)
   - What: remove boilerplate and long instructions; convert examples to compressed bullet patterns; explicit system directives that prefer concision.
   - Metric to capture: delta tokens in request, first-token latency, semantic fidelity score (manual rubric 0–5 for 5 prompts).
   - Quick check: show latency drop on hosted API with no infra change.

2) KV prefix caching for repeated sessions
   - What: if user reuses recent context, store KV (layer-0) snapshot for session and warm on request. Also cache summarized embeddings for long docs.
   - Implementation notes: use Redis-backed KV store with TTL aligned to session; preload before user call; measure cache hit rate.
   - Risk: staleness if user edits earlier utterances — include simple invalidation rule (edit -> invalidate session cache).

3) Shallow quant on candidate variant
   - What: run 8-bit quantized variant (or bfloat16->int8 path) for the baseline model used in demo. Keep fp16/32 as fallback.
   - When: after prompt slimming shows gains and fidelity remains acceptable.
   - Measure: throughput/latency, perplexity diff, diffs on the 5 prompt fidelity rubric.
   - Caveat: watch out for hallucination increase on long-range dependencies.

4) Lossy document compression pipeline
   - Ingest long doc -> split to chunks -> embed -> cluster/summarize top-k -> rehydrate compressed summary to prompt.
   - Tradeoffs: large token savings vs potential context-loss for detail-sensitive tasks (legal/medical). Add QA checks where failing prompts trigger fallback to full context path.
   - Implementation: use small summarizer model (mini LLM) or extractive heuristic + vector store pruning. Keep logs for audit.

5) Adaptive cascade / hybrid precision routing
   - What: route to compact model for high-confidence intents (classification, paraphrase) and to full model for low-confidence generative tasks.
   - Confidence signal: similarity threshold on embeddings, or cheap classifier head.

Checklist for a POC workshop (90–120m):
- Pre-work: obtain 5 canonical user examples + 2 long-context examples from customer; collect latency baseline on hosted API and Dedicated if available.
- Run prompt slimming in shared doc and sync with customer — show before/after token counts.
- Demo caching with synthetic repeated session to prove p50/95 win.
- Toggle quant variant live (if Dedicated or Private available) and show delta.
- Show lossy compression on one long doc path and compare outputs (annotated differences).
- Safety net: run fallback to full model for discrepancy > threshold and log.

Suggested experiments to include in SE playbook (quick perf scripts):
- Single-request latency script that measures first-token and full-response with and without KV warmup.
- Token-saver counter that diff prompt tokenization counts programmatically.
- Fidelity scorer: standardized micro-rubric (answer-correctness, hallucination, completeness, tone) rated by human/quick crowd.

Mini-decision log (example entries):
- 2024-10-15: Decided to prefer prompt slimming before quant to avoid false negatives on fidelity. (owner: Ethan)
- 2024-10-25: Customer X showed hallucination spike at 8-bit; we added per-request fallback to fp16 if hallucination score > 2/5. (owner: Maya)
- 2024-11-02: Implemented prefix-KV warm on Dedicated pool; observed median first-token drop ~32ms on 4k tokens (internal bench). (owner: Jonah)

Prompt-slimming heuristics (practical rules):
- Move example lists to numbered compact forms; use placeholders instead of long sample texts (e.g., [SAMPLE_ORDER_TEXT]).
- Convert natural-language long instructions into structured constraints (one-per-line).
- Avoid repetition and meta-comments inside system message.
- If user-provided context is > 2k tokens, replace with 1–3 bullet summary + embedding-ref.

Quick tech notes (serving/runtime):
- For Dedicated: pin quant variant to a model slot and ensure model-compat kernels are available; use safe-fallback policy in routing config.
- For Hosted: run A/B by routing 10% traffic to quantized variant but allow 100% fallback on mismatch. Capture preds in telemetry.

Observability & telemetry to capture for POC:
- Token counts (prompt+response), first-token latency, tail latency (p95/p99), model variant, kv-cache hit/miss, quant flag, semantic-fidelity tag.
- Attach per-request small checksum of outputs (hash) to detect silent drift across variants.

Demo scripts / commands (SE quick copy):
- Token diff: python tools/token_diff.py --prompt-file examples/a.txt --model gptx-mini
- Warm KV: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/warm -d '{"session_id":"demo-1","kv_snapshot":true}'
- Route test: curl -H "x-variant:quant8" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{...}'

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- Lossy compress dropped critical clause -> mitigation: use QA test for clauses and auto-fallback to full context if fail.
- Quant increases repetition/hallucination -> mitigation: lower beam/temperature and enable fp16 fallback on heuristics.
- Cache staleness after edits -> mitigation: invalidate on edit hook or use version-token mapping.

Open questions for next engineering work:
- Tightening the automatic fidelity metric: we need a cheap classifier that flags semantic divergence without human review.
- Better embedding-based chunk pruning heuristics: when to keep edge sentences versus core summary.
- A small on-device summarizer for Private deployments (OOB2) so that customers in air-gapped env can still compress client-side.

Appendix: demo prompt examples (before / after)
- BEFORE (system): "You are an assistant that must always follow these long instructions: include user persona, 4 examples, style guide, and exhaustive legal disclaimers. Also include the entire user chat transcript."
- AFTER (system): "Assistant: concisely answer user. Follow numbered constraints: 1) factual; 2) concise (<80 words); 3) cite sources if present. Insert [CONTEXT_SUMMARY] and use placeholder samples."

Notes to SEs (tone + delivery):
- Be explicit that we are optimizing for latency and unit-cost trade-offs; show measured deltas and a fallback plan so customers feel safe.
- Use the fidelity rubric as a conversation anchor — customers respond well to transparent scoring.

——
Status / next steps:
- Iterate the experiment scripts, add automated fidelity check pipeline, schedule a dry-run with infra (Dedicated) and customer sample data.

Contact: Ethan Liu (ethan@redwood.ai) — slack #se-pocs for coordination.
